name: Admin
title: Genealogical link between Hezron and Amminadab in Jesus's lineage
summary:
Admin, also known by the name form Arni, appears in Luke's genealogy as the son of Hezron and father of Amminadab.  
He is part of the messianic lineage from Judah through King David and onward to Jesus Christ.  
In the Old Testament genealogies in Ruth and 1 Chronicles, the name Ram is given in the same genealogical position, and the relationship between the names Admin, Arni, and Ram remains a subject of ongoing textual criticism.  
Some manuscripts distinguish between Arni and Admin as two separate generations, which further complicates the issue.  
Although much about this figure remains uncertain, his place in the genealogy illustrates God's faithful preservation of the promised lineage from the patriarchs to the Messiah.
roles: Ancestor in the tribe of Judah

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Jesus's genealogy in Luke
keyEvents.description: In the genealogy of the Gospel of Luke, Admin (Arni) is mentioned as the son of Hezron and father of Amminadab, a link in Jesus's lineage from David back to Judah.

keyEvents.title: Corresponding position in Perez's genealogy in Ruth
keyEvents.description: In the Book of Ruth, Hesron's son Ram (who may correspond to Admin) is listed as the father of Amminadab in the genealogy from Peres to David. The difference between the names Ram and Admin is a subject of textual criticism.

keyEvents.title: Parallel in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles, Ram is mentioned as the son of Hesron and the father of Amminadab, occupying the same genealogical position that Admin holds in the Gospel of Luke. This is one of the central parallels in the discussion about the identity of Admin/Ram.

keyEvents.title: The Connection Between Hesron and Amminadab
keyEvents.description: Admin serves as the genealogical link between Hesron, grandson of Judah, and Amminadab, who became the father of Nahshon—a leader of the tribe of Judah during the wilderness wanderings.

keyEvents.title: Part of Christ's Royal Lineage
keyEvents.description: Through Admin runs the royal line from the tribe of Judah that fulfills Jacob's prophecy that the scepter shall not depart from Judah.

versions.summary: Admin (also spelled Arni) was a descendant of Judah and an ancestor of King David, and thus also of Jesus Christ. He is mentioned in the genealogies in the Book of Ruth and in the Gospel of Luke as an important link in the messianic lineage.
versions.title: Descendant of Hesron
versions.reason: [major] Admin likely lived in the period between the patriarchs and the Exodus, or possibly during the Egyptian period. Technically, he is placed genealogically between Judah (the patriarchal era) and Nahshon (who lived during the Exodus). 'Patriarchs' is acceptable but debatable; nevertheless, it is the closest available era.; [minor] The term 'patriarch' is somewhat misleading for Admin, who is primarily known as a link in a genealogy. 'Ancestor in the tribe of Judah' or 'Descendant in the tribe of Judah' would be more precise. He has no documented leadership role.; [major] Ruth 4:19 mentions that Hezron was the father of Ram (not Admin). The name 'Admin' does not appear in Ruth 4:19. It is Luke 3:33 that mentions Admin/Arni. The text of Ruth uses the name Ram. There is a textual-critical discussion about whether Admin and Ram are the same person or different persons, but to claim that Admin is mentioned by name in Ruth 4:19 is imprecise.; [minor] Numbers 1:7 mentions Amminadab as the father of Nahshon, but does not mention Admin directly. The reference is relevant as context, but it should be clarified that Admin is not explicitly named here.; [minor] The summary should clarify the textual-critical variation: Admin/Arni is mentioned primarily in Luke 3:33, while Ruth 4:19 and 1 Chronicles 2:9–10 use the name Ram. The relationship between Admin and Ram is debated.; [minor] The title 'Descendant of Hezron' is somewhat vague. 'Son of Hezron in Jesus's genealogy' or 'Hezron's son and ancestor of David' would have been more informative.

versions.summary: Admin (also known as Arni) is mentioned in the genealogy of the Gospel of Luke as the son of Hesron and the father of Amminadab, thus serving as a link in the messianic line from Judah to King David and onward to Jesus Christ. In the Old Testament genealogies in Ruth and Chronicles, the name Ram is used in the corresponding position, and the relationship between Admin and Ram is debated among scholars. Regardless, Admin represents an important link in God's redemptive plan.
versions.title: Hesron's Son in Jesus' Lineage
versions.reason: [major] Admin likely lived in the period between the patriarchs and the Exodus from Egypt, but since he is placed between Hesron (grandson of Jacob/Israel) and Amminadab (whose grandson Nahshon was a leader during the wilderness wanderings), 'patriarchs' fits reasonably well. Still, one could argue that the period overlaps with the beginning of the stay in Egypt. We keep 'patriarchs' as it is the closest alternative.; [minor] The title 'Hesron's son in Jesus' genealogy' is accurate but somewhat flat. It could be made slightly more descriptive to highlight his role as a genealogical link.; [minor] The summary is good and informative, but the final sentence ('Admin represents anyway an important link') can be tightened to avoid the somewhat vague 'anyway'.; [minor] The third key event ('Part of the messianic line') refers to Ruth 4:18–22, but Admin/Arni is not mentioned explicitly here—it is Ram who is named. The description should clarify that this is the parallel genealogy in which Ram (possibly equivalent to Admin) appears.; [minor] Some scholars hold that Luke has Admin as the father of Arni (or vice versa), and that Amminadab is a child of Arni, not directly of Admin. Text-critical uncertainty makes this difficult to determine, but the current arrangement with Amminadab as Admin's son follows the most common reading and is acceptable.

versions.summary:
Admin, also known by the name form Arni, is mentioned in Luke's genealogy as the son of Hezron and father of Amminadab.  
He thus forms a link in the messianic lineage from Judah through King David to Jesus Christ.  
In the Old Testament genealogies in Ruth and 1 Chronicles, the name Ram is given in the same genealogical position, and the relationship between Admin and Ram is subject to textual-critical and research-based discussion.  
Regardless of the naming question, Admin serves as an important connecting link in the salvation-historical line that God maintains from the patriarchs to the Messiah.
versions.title: Genealogical link between Hezron and Amminadab in Jesus's lineage
versions.reason: [minor] Some textual critics read Luke 3:33 so that Admin and Arni are two separate generations (Hesron → Arni → Admin → Amminadab). In that case, Admin's father would be Arni, not Hesron. The profile follows a reasonable reading, but it could have been clearer that this is disputed.; [minor] The summary is well formulated, but the last two sentences are somewhat repetitive – both emphasize the connective function. A slight rephrasing could provide more variety and information density.; [minor] There is no footnote on how rabbinic or Jewish tradition handles variations in the genealogy. A footnote on this would give broader coverage.

footnotes.text: The name Admin (or Arni) appears in Luke 3:33 in several Greek manuscripts, but there is significant textual variation. Some manuscripts have 'Admin', others 'Arni', and some combine both as two separate generations. The Hebrew genealogy in Ruth 4:19 and 1 Chronicles 2:9–10 uses the name 'Ram' in the corresponding position.

The relationship between Admin/Arni and Ram is debated among scholars. Some believe they are the same person with different name forms, while others argue that Luke preserves a more detailed genealogy where Admin/Arni represents an extra generation omitted from the Old Testament genealogies.

Hesron, Admin's father, was the grandson of Judah and Tamar (through Peres). This lineage held special theological significance as the tribe to which the scepter was promised according to Genesis 49:10, ultimately leading to King David and Jesus Christ.

Nahshon, who was Admin's grandson through Amminadab, was the leader of the tribe of Judah during the wilderness wanderings (Num 1:7; 2:3). This shows that the lineage through Admin held a prominent position in Israel's early history.

The oldest and most reliable Greek manuscripts, including Codex Vaticanus (B) and Codex Sinaiticus (א), have varying readings in Luke 3:33. Papyrus 75 (P75), one of the earliest manuscripts of the Gospel of Luke, supports the reading 'Admin' and 'Arni' as two separate names, which has led many textual critics to prefer this reading.

In rabbinic tradition and early Jewish genealogies (such as in the Targums and midrash literature), Hesron's son is identified exclusively as Ram, with no reference to the form Admin or Arni. The Greek name form may represent a translation variant or an independent tradition that Luke had access to.
